marketSegment: Self-hosted running analytics and coaching platforms

topCompetitors.name: Strava
topCompetitors.position: Dominant social fitness network (120M+ users), IPO-bound. Lacks VDOT science, injury prediction, self-hosted.

topCompetitors.name: Runalyze
topCompetitors.position: Closest feature competitor — Effective VO2max, shoe tracking, race prediction. SaaS-only, no injury prediction or daily recs.

topCompetitors.name: TrainingPeaks
topCompetitors.position: Gold standard for coach-athlete workflow. No running-specific physiology models, no self-hosted.

opportunities.title: Self-hosted deployment as core differentiator
opportunities.rationale: Zero competitors offer self-hosted deployment. Privacy concerns rising (Strava oversharing campaign, Garmin Connect+ backlash). r/selfhosted has 748K subscribers explicitly wanting fitness analytics. This is Hermes' strongest moat.

opportunities.title: One-command Docker deployment for non-technical users
opportunities.rationale: Social signal shows non-technical users want self-hosted fitness analytics but are blocked by Docker/Linux expertise. Lowering this barrier expands SOM significantly.
opportunities.effort: Medium — compose file, documentation, guided setup

opportunities.title: VDOT science + daily training recommendations as premium differentiator
opportunities.rationale: No competitor implements Jack Daniels' VDOT model for automated daily training. Users want science-backed, actionable guidance — not just raw data. This is a clear positioning gap.
opportunities.effort: Already implemented — refine UI and onboarding

opportunities.title: SEO content strategy targeting 'Strava alternative' and 'self-hosted fitness' keywords
opportunities.rationale: 'Strava alternative' has 27K monthly searches with low competition for open-source/self-hosted variants. 'Self-hosted fitness tracker' (1.6K/mo, low difficulty). Creating comparison guides and free tools could drive significant organic traffic.
opportunities.effort: Medium — blog posts, free VDOT calculator, comparison pages

opportunities.title: Predictive injury risk scoring (training load + HRV + biomechanics)
opportunities.rationale: No competitor offers predictive injury analytics — only reactive tracking (Final Surge PAIR) or readiness scores (WHOOP, Garmin). ACWR + cadence drift + cardiac drift modeling is unique. Users actively want injury prevention signals.
opportunities.effort: Already partially implemented — promote and validate

opportunities.title: Go-to-market as 'privacy-first running analytics'
opportunities.rationale: Data sovereignty sentiment is surging (Garmin 'don't become Fitbit' post has 2K+ upvotes). Strava's own privacy campaigns confirm user concern. 'Privacy focused fitness tracker' has 900 monthly searches with low SEO difficulty. Position as the self-hosted, no-spyware alternative.
opportunities.effort: Low — positioning and landing page copy

opportunities.title: Shoe tracking with predictive mileage alerts and brand recommendations
opportunities.rationale: Runalyze tracks shoe mileage but lacks proactive replacement alerts. Shoe-health correlation with performance is unique. Low effort to enhance existing feature. Potential for affiliate revenue.

opportunities.title: 3-tier pricing: Free → Pro $8/mo ($79/yr) → Team $12/mo
opportunities.rationale: Strava at $11.99/mo sets ceiling. Runalyze at €5.50/mo proves analytics-heavy platforms succeed at lower tiers. $8/mo undercuts Strava by 33% while justifying premium over Intervals.icu ($4/mo). Annual $79/yr matches 'under $100' psychological anchor. Team tier creates expansion revenue.

opportunities.title: Free interactive VDOT calculator as SEO lead magnet
opportunities.rationale: 'VDOT training calculator' has 4.8K monthly searches with medium difficulty. A free, embeddable tool would attract high-intent traffic, earn backlinks, and showcase Hermes' science accuracy. Tool-based SEO is a proven link-building strategy.

opportunities.title: Integration with Apple Watch and COROS beyond Garmin
opportunities.rationale: Wearables market growing at 12.1% CAGR ($92.9B). COROS is 3rd in GPS watches and growing fast. Apple Watch has largest smartwatch base. Vendor-agnostic import is a strong differentiator from Garmin Connect (Garmin-only). Currently Hermes syncs best with Garmin.

opportunities.title: Cross-training load unification across sports
opportunities.rationale: Racket sports +67%, strength +29%, HIIT +45% growth. No platform unifies running + strength + other sports into one body-load score. Users currently wear Whoop + Garmin simultaneously.

opportunities.title: White-label for coaching businesses (branded Hermes instances)
opportunities.rationale: Coaches pay $50-200+/mo for athletic platforms. Self-hosted white-label instance with 50 athletes included at $29-49/mo could capture coaching market. TrainingPeaks lacks self-hosted. Final Surge lacks VDOT science.

opportunities.title: Programmatic SEO for race-specific training pages
opportunities.rationale: City + marathon training content (e.g., 'Boston Marathon training with analytics') targets race-seasonal search traffic. Low effort per page with template approach. Limited by domain authority.

opportunities.title: Training plan marketplace with coach-created plans
opportunities.rationale: Additional revenue stream via 70/30 creator split. TrainingPeaks model validated. Requires critical mass of coach users first. Low priority until user base grows.

opportunities.title: Physio/clinic integration for injury prediction reports
opportunities.rationale: B2B revenue opportunity but requires HIPAA compliance, clinical validation, and sales team. High effort for uncertain return at current stage.
